digest.component_or_area: rebar Jira DC reconciler live verification suite
propositions: The epic's headline AC — a DC-created issue appears locally after an inbound pass and a local edit appears on the DC issue after an outbound pass — is proven live in both directions against a real Jira 8.17.1 Data Center instance over a scrubbed copy of the real production ticket store.

Live verification must run against a copy of the real ticket store fetched from the orphan gitignored tickets branch and extracted into .tickets-tracker/, isolated in a fresh repo with no git remote plus REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=off and no Cloud credentials, asserted rather than assumed.

The store copy must be scrubbed of all .bridge_state* binding and snapshot artifacts (matched by glob, enumerated from the tree, including the .bak-retarget backup) so the reconciler cannot form intent to write to production Jira keys.

Assertions must measure the correct side of the bridge and never rely on aggregate 'converged' lines: scanned counts remote issues not local tickets, and each mutation must round-trip against a named per-mutation oracle, with set_parent's epic case asserted directly against the transport via NotImplementedError.

A product defect exists where transition_issue_by_name matches a transition's name rather than its destination status, causing silent partial status-sync failures on DC (in_progress fails while closed works by coincidence), fixed by resolving against to.name.

Ambiguous single assertions repeatedly masked distinct root causes (filter dropped inbound creates, bundled idempotence produced false reds, oracle read identity off the ticket instead of the registry); splitting assertions into their own cells localised each fault.
